mainText:
Special votes have been counted and New Zealand's election result is due at two o'clock today, with the final seat count deciding who governs.

New Zealand.

Final special vote results are released this afternoon. About four hundred thousand special votes were outstanding, roughly fourteen per cent of all votes cast. Newsroom and RNZ both report the next government hangs by a thread, with pollster David Farrar warning a weeks-long recount is possible if the last seat is close between the two blocs. The Opportunity Party remains below the five per cent threshold and needs an electorate seat to return. Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins are both waiting on the same numbers.

RNZ says it is still managing an attempted cyber breach, working with specialist security providers. The Public Service Association says it will file legal action next week unless RNZ halts plans to cut fifty eight jobs, and wants a wider review of the broadcaster's finances after its HR boss departed. Plans to also cut the Asia, business and technology teams have widened the dispute, with the Rural Communities Minister calling related cuts to rural reporting extremely disappointing.

Health New Zealand has rehired at least one hundred and sixty six workers made redundant since the agency formed in twenty twenty two. The figure does not include staff who returned as contractors, and raises questions about whether the original cuts were properly planned.

Internal Affairs has written off twenty three million dollars on a civil registration technology project. The births, deaths and marriages system relies on twenty five year old unreliable technology guarding eighty million records, and a revised replacement plan has been judged too risky to proceed.

Consumer confidence has climbed back above the key one hundred mark, its highest level since January, as fuel prices ease.

In the Bay of Plenty, biosecurity investigators have captured a live adult male cane toad near a lake at Tauriko, after it was caught on video. The toad is poisonous and invasive, and officials are checking for others in the area. A Far North code of conduct hearing involving all councillors is set down as a day long public session, livestreamed because seating is capped at twenty.

World.

Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting eleven thousand jobs at risk after its owners failed to find a buyer. A new chief executive has separately been appointed to lead Travelodge from the first of December.

Norse Atlantic has suspended all flights and is seeking urgent funding, warning it will file for bankruptcy without a financial lifeline.

A diesel tanker carrying up to seven thousand tonnes has capsized near Ibiza, killing one person. Spain's sea rescue service is still assessing possible environmental damage.

Nine people have been injured, three critically, after an explosion at a Bangkok oil refinery, with black smoke visible across the city skyline.

Major Thanksgiving storms have brought flooding and flight delays across both American coasts, with wind gusts, downed trees and power outages affecting hundreds of thousands of customers.

Technology.

Nvidia shares have risen by almost one trillion dollars in value as tech stocks rallied following Jensen Huang's return as chief executive, lifting the Nasdaq by six and a half per cent. The United States attorney general has still not confirmed whether Huang remains under investigation, and lawmakers continue demanding answers about Donald Trump's role in his reinstatement. BBC analysts note the fears over an AI bubble that existed before Huang's exit have not gone away.

The United States has approved Elon Musk's SpaceX plan to launch up to a million data satellites for AI computing power, a project astronomers say could alter the night sky and atmosphere. Mexico has raised separate concerns with Washington about suspected SpaceX rocket debris near its border with Texas.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks have made six changes for Saturday's rematch with England at Twickenham. Coach Dave Rennie says last weekend hurt but there is an opportunity to go again against a quality side. Jordie Barrett is confirmed as captain, described by Rennie as a straightforward decision.

Cricket. The Black Caps and India are into day one of the second test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Devon Conway was out on the cusp of lunch. India's Rishabh Pant had earlier turned out for a Christchurch club match under a false name and scored fifty four from twenty one balls. Paceman Jacob Duffy is expected to again carry a heavy bowling load.

Boxing. Joseph Parker fights WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois in his comeback bout, his first fight since a loss last October. It will be his first world title shot since twenty seventeen, and pundits say ring rust could count against him.

Formula One. Liam Lawson says he is less experienced than he appears after another difficult season, ahead of this season's remaining rounds.

Rugby league. State of Origin tickets at Eden Park have almost sold out, with remaining seats priced between three hundred and four hundred and fifty two dollars.

Coming up. Election results due at two o'clock today. The All Blacks play England at Twickenham this weekend. The Black Caps continue day one in Christchurch today. Joseph Parker fights Daniel Dubois for the WBO heavyweight title.

End of flash.
